Cloud computing is the on-demand delivery of IT resources (servers, storage, databases) over the internet with pay-as-you-go pricing, managed by providers like AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure. It eliminates the need for local hardware maintenance, offering high scalability, flexibility, and remote access to data from any device. How Cloud Computing Works Instead of storing data or running applications on a local computer or office server, you connect to remote data centers managed by cloud providers. Internet Dependence: Access requires an internet connection. Virtualization: Providers use virtualization to slice physical servers into multiple virtual machines. Usage-Based: Users rent resources, allowing them to scale up or down instantly. Key Characteristics On-Demand Self-Service: Resources are available automatically without human intervention. Broad Network Access: Services are accessible over the internet via mobile devices, laptops, and workstations. Resource Pooling: Provider resources serve multiple users (multi-tenant). Rapid Elasticity: Capabilities can be scaled up or down rapidly based on demand. Measured Service: Usage is metered and charged based on consumption (pay-as-you-go). Types of Cloud Computing (Service Models) IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service): Rents infrastructure like servers and virtual machines (e.g., AWS, Azure). PaaS (Platform as a Service): Provides a platform for developers to build and deploy apps. SaaS (Software as a Service): Delivers software applications over the internet (e.g., Google Drive, Salesforce, Netflix). Types of Cloud Deployment Public Cloud: Services delivered over the public internet and shared across organizations. Private Cloud: Computing resources used exclusively by one business. Hybrid Cloud: A combination of public and private clouds, allowing data and apps to be shared between them. Benefits Cost Efficiency: No upfront hardware costs; pay only for what you use. Scalability: Instantly increase or decrease computing capacity. Accessibility: Access data and apps from anywhere in the world. Security & Backup: Automated backups and advanced security measures, such as iCloud Private Relay or data encryption, improve data protection. iCloud Private Relay Challenges and Risks Security & Hacking: While providers offer high security, data can be vulnerable to breaches. Internet Dependence: Cannot access data without a connection. Uncertainty: Reliance on third-party provider performance and availability. Common examples include storing photos in iCloud or Google Photos, using Microsoft 365 for work, or streaming on Netflix. iCloud Google Photos Microsoft 365 Netflix
